questions.solution:
The equation of the given curve is $\mathrm{y}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}-3}, \mathrm{x} \neq 3$

The slope of the tangent to the given curve

at any point $(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y})$ is given by $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\frac{-1}{(\mathrm{x}-3)^{2}}$

For tangent having slope $2,$ we must have

$2=\frac{-1}{(x-3)^{2}}$

\Rightarrow 2(x-3)^{2}=-1 \Rightarrow(x-3)^{2}=-\frac{1}{2}



which is not possible as square of a real number cannot be negative. Hence, there is no tangent to the given curve having slope 2 .

questions.q: If the real part of $\frac{\bar{z}+2}{\bar{z}-1}$ is $4, z \neq 1,$ then the locus of the point representing $z$ in the complex plane is
options: a straight line equally inclined to axes
questions.solution:
Real part of $\frac{\bar{z}+2}{\bar{z}-1}$ is given by



\begin{array}{l}

\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{\bar{z}+2}{\bar{z}-1}+\left(\frac{\bar{z}+2}{\bar{z}-1}\right)\right]=4 \\

\Rightarrow \frac{\bar{z}+2}{\bar{z}-1}+\frac{z+2}{z-1}=8 \\

\Rightarrow z \bar{z}-\bar{z}+2 z-2+z \bar{z}+2 \bar{z}-z-2 \\

=8(z \bar{z}-\bar{z}-z+1) \\

\Rightarrow z \bar{z}-\frac{3}{2} z-\frac{3}{2} \bar{z}+2=0

\end{array}



Comparing with the equation $z \bar{z}+\bar{a} z+a \bar{z}+b=0,$ we get $a=-\frac{3}{2}$ and $b=2$. Thus, the locus of $z$ given by the equation

(i) is a circle with centre $=\frac{1}{2}$

Thus $\alpha^{100}=(-\omega)^{100}=\omega$ and

$\beta^{100}=\left(-\omega^{2}\right)^{100}=\omega^{2},$ so that the required

equation is $\mathrm{x}^{2}+\mathrm{x}+1=0$

\left|\begin{array}{ccc}

\left.-(x-5)(x-3)^{2}\right\}+(x-3)(x-4)^{2} \\

\Rightarrow(x-4)(x-5)(x-5-x+4) \\

-(x-3)(x-5)(x-5-x+3) \\

$(x-4)=0$

\Rightarrow-x^{2}+9 x-20+2 x^{2}-16 x+30-x^{2}+7 x-12=0



$\Rightarrow-32+30=0 \Rightarrow-2=0$

Which is not possible, hence no value of $\mathrm{x}$ satisfies the given condition.
